content.text: After discussion with

, it seems that more useful than this would be a set of patterns for the tasks to which people try to put blank nodes, like ordering or paired values. I can either close this Won't Fix and open a new ticket or edit this ticket.
Feel free to edit this ticket. Thanks,

, I agree the patterns will be useful. But also useful would be a short lifecycle discussion, and how blank nodes don't have an easily defined lifecycle whereas hash-uris do. When you taught me that, it was key to getting me off the blank node path.

Okay, that's fair-- but where? That doesn't belong directly in the API documentation. I think perhaps we should do the section of patterns, and general notes about the werkgeist of blank nodes in LDP should go there as prefatory material.
To keep this task manageable, you could simply create an FAQ page describing Fedora's relationship with bnodes as a child of:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Fedora+4.x+Documentation
Under
How-Tos
Under FAQ:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/FAQs+and+How-Tos
Right, I'm asking if I can open a new subsection under
How-Tos
, in that page, something like "Common Metadata Design Patterns".
Sure
, please take a quick look at:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Common+metadata+design+patterns
and see if that note captures the information that was of value to you. Thanks!
, there is now a page in that section for discussing ordering:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Ordering
Please add your experience to it!

, this ticket has clearly morphed. I'm going to close it, but if you want to open another for "document design patterns" or something, that's fine with me. Otherwise, I feel like filling out that new section of the wiki is going to happen over time, not as a single task.
Thanks,
. It will be good to get
's thoughts.
It will also be valuable to to community to get these three stub pages fleshed out:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Ordering
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Date+and+time+ranges
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Paired+values
Do you plan on doing that over time? Do you actually have these patterns?
I don't think we yet know what the right patterns
are
. I think we need to "let a hundred flowers bloom". Or at least some morning glory.
I really like what you've done,
. I'll work on adding some ordering flowers. I've been exploring different ways of doing ordering and I want to actually try them in Fedora, so this is a good prompt for me.
This task is to document the design and rationale for Fedora's relationship with blank nodes.

comments.body: After discussion with Martin Haye, it seems that more useful than this would be a set of patterns for the tasks to which people try to put blank nodes, like ordering or paired values. I can either close this Won't Fix and open a new ticket or edit this ticket.
Feel free to edit this ticket. Thanks, A. Soroka.

A. Soroka, I agree the patterns will be useful. But also useful would be a short lifecycle discussion, and how blank nodes don't have an easily defined lifecycle whereas hash-uris do. When you taught me that, it was key to getting me off the blank node path.

Okay, that's fair-- but where? That doesn't belong directly in the API documentation. I think perhaps we should do the section of patterns, and general notes about the werkgeist of blank nodes in LDP should go there as prefatory material.

To keep this task manageable, you could simply create an FAQ page describing Fedora's relationship with bnodes as a child of:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Fedora+4.x+Documentation
Right, I'm asking if I can open a new subsection under How-Tos, in that page, something like "Common Metadata Design Patterns".

Martin Haye, please take a quick look at:

https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Common+metadata+design+patterns

and see if that note captures the information that was of value to you. Thanks!

Martin Haye, there is now a page in that section for discussing ordering:

https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Ordering

Please add your experience to it!

Andrew Woods, this ticket has clearly morphed. I'm going to close it, but if you want to open another for "document design patterns" or something, that's fine with me. Otherwise, I feel like filling out that new section of the wiki is going to happen over time, not as a single task.

Thanks, A. Soroka. It will be good to get Martin Haye's thoughts.
It will also be valuable to to community to get these three stub pages fleshed out:

  • https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Ordering
  • https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Date+and+time+ranges
  • https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Paired+values

Do you plan on doing that over time? Do you actually have these patterns?
I don't think we yet know what the right patterns are. I think we need to "let a hundred flowers bloom". Or at least some morning glory.

I really like what you've done, A. Soroka. I'll work on adding some ordering flowers. I've been exploring different ways of doing ordering and I want to actually try them in Fedora, so this is a good prompt for me.
